<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par55 />{{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹרַשׁ}}, ''denominative'' from {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁ֫רֶשׁ|translate=root}} (but {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁרֵשׁ|translate=to root out}}); in Hithpôʿēl {{GHGheb|text=הִתְגּֽׄעֲשׁוּ|translate=they shall be moved}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=16}}; imperf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=8|hidebook=1}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹשֵׂ֫תִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=13}}. The {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מִנֹּאָץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=5}} is probably a ''forma mixta'' combining the readings {{GHGheb|text=מְנֹאָץ}} and {{GHGheb|text=מִתְנֹאֵץ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|c}}
''Poʿel'' proper (as distinguished from the corresponding conjugations of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} {{GHGpar|67|l}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} {{GHGpar|72|m}}, which take the place of the ordinary causative {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}) expresses an aim or endeavour to perform the action, especially with hostile intent, and is hence called, by Ewald, the stem expressing ''aim'' (Zielstamm), ''endeavour'' (Suche-stamm) or ''attack'' (Angriffs-stamm); cf. the examples given above from {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=101|verse=5}}, and {{GHGheb|text=עוֹיֵן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=9}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (probably for {{GHGheb|text=מְעוֹיֵן}}, cf. {{GHGpar|52|s}}; {{GHGpar|55|f}}: ''seeking to cast an evil eye'').

With {{GHGheb|text=קוֹטֵל}} is connected the formation of quadriliterals by the insertion of a consonant between the first and second radicals ({{GHGpar|30|p}}, § 56).

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|d}}
2. ''Paʿlēl'', generally with the ''ă'' attenuated to ''ĭ''=''Piʿlēl''<ref>Cf. Wolfensohn, ‘The Piʿlel in Hebrew,’ ''Amer. Journ. of Or. Studies'', xxvii (1907), p. 303 ff.</ref> (''Piʿlal''), {{GHGheb|text=קִטְלֵל}} and {{GHGheb|text=קִטְלַל}}; the ''ē'' in the final syllable also arises from ''ĭ'', and this again from ''ă''; passive ''Puʿlal'' {{GHGheb|text=קֻטְלַל}}, reflexive ''Hithpaʿlēl'' {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקַטְלֵל}}, like the Arabic conjugations ix. ''ʾiqtăllă'' and xi. ''ʾiqtâllă'', the former used of permanent, the latter of accidental or changing conditions, e.g. of colours; cf. {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׁאֲנַן|translate=to be at rest}}, {{GHGheb|text=רַֽעֲנַן|translate=to be green}}, passive {{GHGheb|text=אֻמְלַל|translate=to be withered}}, all of them found only in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and with no corresponding {{GHGterm|Qal}} form. (For the barbarous form {{GHGheb|text=צִמְּתֻת֫וּנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=88|verse=17}} read {{GHGheb|text=צִמְתָֽתְנִי}}; for {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=23}}, which has manifestly arisen only from confusion with the following {{GHGheb|text=חלל}}, read {{GHGheb|text=נָפַל}}). These forms are more common in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, where they take the place of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} ({{GHGpar|72|m}}). Cf. also {{GHGpar|75|kk}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|e}}
3. ''P<sup>e</sup>ʿalʿal'': {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְטַל}} with repetition of the last two radicals, used of movements repeated in quick succession; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סְחַרְחַר|translate=to go about quickly, to palpitate}} (of the heart) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=11}}, from {{GHGheb|text=סָחַר|translate=to go about}}; passive {{GHGheb|text=חֳמַרְמַר|translate=to be in a ferment, to be heated, to be red}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=11|hidebook=1}}. Probably this is also the explanation of {{GHGheb|text=חֲצוֹצַר}} (denom. from {{GHGheb|text=חֲצֽוֹצְרָה|translate=a trumpet}}, but only in the {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=24}} &c. {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}) for {{GHGheb|text=חֲצַרְצַר}}, by absorption of the first {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, lengthening of ''ă'' in the open syllable, and subsequent obscuring of ''ā'' to ''ô''. On the other hand, for the meaningless {{GHGheb|text=אָֽהֲבוּ הֵב֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=4|verse=18}} (which could only be referred to this conjugation if it stood for {{GHGheb|text=אֲהַבְהֲבוּ}}) read {{GHGheb|text=אָֽהֲבוּ}}, and for the equally meaningless {{GHGheb|text=יָפְיָפִ֫יתָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=3}} read {{GHGheb|text=יָפִ֫יתָ}}. In both these cases a scribal error (''dittography'') has been perpetuated by the punctuation, which did not venture to alter the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}. On the employment of ''P<sup>e</sup>ʿalʿal'' in the formation of nouns, cf. {{GHGpar|84|n|b}}. Closely related to this form is—

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|f}}
4. ''Pilpēl'' (pass. ''Pŏlpal''), with a strengthening of the two essential radicals in stems {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, and {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גִּלְגֵּל|translate=to roll}}, from {{GHGheb|text=גַּל}}={{GHGheb|text=גָּלַל}}; {{GHGterm|reflexive}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְגַּלְגֵּל|translate=to roll oneself down}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּלְכֵּל}} from {{GHGheb|text=כּוּל}}, {{GHGterm|passive}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּלְכַּל}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=טֵאטֵא}} (so Baer and Ginsb. after Qimḥi; others {{GHGheb|text=טִאטֵא}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=23}}, and with ''ă'' in both syllables owing to the influence of {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַרְקַר}} from {{GHGheb|text=קוּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=17}} (cf. however, in the parallel passage, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=45}} {{GHGheb|text=קָדְקֹד}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=5}}, in the {{GHGterm|participle}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׂגְשֵׂג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=11}} ''to hedge in'', acc. to others ''make to grow''. Probably to this form also belongs {{GHGheb|text=יְלַעְלְעוּ}}, the emended reading of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=39|verse=30}} instead of the impossible {{GHGheb|text=יְעַלְעוּ}}; also<section end=par54 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
